title: Sara Duterte camp says 2 former staff now safe amid alleged threats
summary: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte said Wednesday that her two former staff who sought help due to alleged threats to their lives are now safe and sound.

blocks.text: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte said Wednesday that her two former staff who sought help due to alleged threats to their lives are now safe and sound.
In a post on Facebook, Atty. Salvador Paolo Panelo, Duterte's spokesperson, said they were able to rescue the two with the help of the police on Tuesday.

"Yesterday (November 17, 2026), the Vice President’s legal team, with police assistance, fetched them and brought them to a police station where they executed affidavits and filed a police blotter," he said.
"For now, the apparent plan to use these individuals for false testimony against the Vice President has been foiled," he added.

He said the two were recruited and engaged by a private individual to work as employees at a resort in Boracay sometime in October. They were then brought to Manila under the pretext of training for their roles.
Panelo said that on November 16, the supposed employer informed the two of the threats to their lives, and that there was also a threat to the employer’s own life because he was “harboring” them.

"The employer then told them that the threats would be quelled if they executed affidavits, drafts of which were presented to them. According to the two individuals, the affidavits contained false allegations against the Vice President, which they refused to sign," he added.
He further said that later that day, one of them reached out to the Vice President for "assistance to extricate themselves from the situation and for safe passage."
Panelo said the two clarified that they were not held in captivity, but they were afraid to leave the employer’s custody due to the supposed threat to their lives.
He said that, for the safety of those involved, they will not provide any further details about the matter.
Malacañang on Tuesday called for an investigation into the claims.

The National Bureau of Investigation, Philippine National Police, and House impeachment trial spokesperson Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, meanwhile, urged Duterte's camp to file a formal report over the alleged threats. —AOL, GMA News
